result: Verdict: **reject**. I read the standing dispatch-prompt rules, then live-tested the shipped guard against a fixture harness. Round 3's claimed fixes (hardcoded `/proc/self/cgroup`, `+` stripping, multi-refspec checking) all genuinely work and are backed by real tests. But I found and confirmed live a complete, undisclosed bypass: the git wrapper only checks `$1 = "push"`, so any standard git global option before the subcommand — `git -C . push origin master` or `git -c user.name=x push origin master` — shifts the subcommand out of `$1` and the push goes straight to the real `git` unblocked. This is the exact class of bug this task exists to close, and it wasn't caught. `review-verdict.json` is written with the full details; no workflow files were touched, and I made no other repo/git changes.
